## Overview

Enable attention sinks with a quantized KV cache on the FlashInfer backend: NVFP4 KV is served by the plain fa2 paged prefill wrapper at `return_lse=True` with the sink applied exactly as an epilogue rescale `out * sigmoid(ln2 * lse - sinks)` (new, SM12x-only), and fp8 KV is unblocked by the same non-bf16 routing in flint's model code. This unblocks quantized weight+KV GGUF models with learned sinks (e.g. RecursiveSI/flint) on RTX 50-series, requested in #63605.

## Claims

- `has_sinks + kv_cache_dtype="nvfp4"` now serves on the fa2 NVFP4 path **on SM12x only**, gated on the *resolved* decode kernel: XQA decode applies sinks natively, but where the builder would revert to the plain fa2 decode wrapper (unsupported head_dim, DCP, non-divisible GQA) setup raises — a direct probe on flashinfer 0.7.2.post1 shows that wrapper's `sinks=` is silently ignored (bit-identical output with or without sinks). SM8x/90 rejections, the head_size-64 rejection, and the nvfp4_trtllm/SM100 path are untouched.
- RecursiveSI/flint NVFP4 GGUF serves end-to-end on RTX 5090 with GSM8K parity vs bf16 (strict 0.4989 vs 0.5087, < 1 stderr). **KV capacity ×3.55 at TP=4** (3.13M → 11.12M tokens; concurrency for 209,632-token requests 14.91× → 53.02×); at TP=1 it enables max-model-len 262144 that bf16 cannot even initialize.
- **fp8 KV also works with no extra code** (routing keyed on any non-bf16 dtype): GSM8K parity (0.5186), 424,435-token pool at TP=1 / 6.25M at TP=4, and on the 9-point TP4 grid below fp8 matches or beats bf16 at 5/9 points — including 131k×32, where nvfp4 pays −21%. Its two regressions (−25% at 16384×8, −43% at 32768×32, each reproduced in a second run) are prefill-side via the pre-existing fmha_v2 fp8 sink-prefill wrapper, not this PR (the new epilogue is nvfp4-only).
- Cost, opt-in only: nvfp4 is −8% to −21% out tok/s on the 5090 grid (fa2 JIT dequantizes fp4 in-kernel; SM120 has no tuned fp4 attention kernel — trtllm-gen fp4 is SM100+). Default `kv_cache_dtype="auto"` paths are untouched. On bandwidth-limited SM120 cards the tradeoff flips positive — see the independent 5060 Ti reproduction in Validation.

## Validation

- Unit tests (`pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py -k nvfp4` on 8× RTX 5090 at this tip: **7 passed, 156 deselected, 33.61s**): `test_flashinfer_nvfp4_sink_prefill_correctness` matches a bf16 `BatchAttentionWithAttentionSinkWrapper` oracle at 2e-2 over a mixed batch (long-context 1-token incremental + pure prefills + long-context short extend), eager and under CUDA graph capture — on main, the same test fails at setup with the pre-existing `NotImplementedError: FlashInfer backend currently does not support attention sinks`; `test_flashinfer_nvfp4_sink_prefill_rejected_without_xqa` asserts the builder raises for NVFP4+sinks when XQA cannot serve the model (GQA 6/4 non-divisible) instead of silently decoding without sinks; plus the 4 pre-existing NVFP4 decode params.
- CI coverage: the dgx-spark step in `.buildkite/test_areas/attention.yaml` is widened from `-k nvfp4_decode_correctness` to `-k "nvfp4_decode_correctness or nvfp4_sink_prefill"` so the two new sink tests run there too (7 selected in total; the selector itself was repaired from a stale name by #64107). Off-SM12x CI pools skip.
- GSM8K, 1319 samples, `lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks gsm8k --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn` (max_gen_toks 2048, temp 0, concurrency 16), against `vllm serve flint-nvfp4.gguf --hf-config-path RecursiveSI/flint` on 1× RTX 5090:

| kv_cache_dtype | gsm8k strict | stderr |
|---|---|---|
| auto (bf16) | 0.5087 | ±0.0138 |
| nvfp4 | 0.4989 | ±0.0138 |
| fp8 | 0.5186 | ±0.0138 |

- Serving A/B on 4× RTX 5090 per side (TP=4, `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, `--ignore-eos`, 128-token outputs). Output tok/s, Δ vs bf16 inline:

  *Note: TP≥4 serving additionally requires the flint silu TP-shard fix, [#63986](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63986), not part of this PR. These numbers were collected with an equivalent fallback applied symmetrically to all three dtypes; relative deltas hold.*

| ISL × conc | bf16 | nvfp4 | fp8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 × 1 | 137.2 | 126.2 (−8%) | 138.4 (+1%) |
| 4096 × 8 | 443.7 | 366.6 (−17%) | 392.6 (−12%) |
| 4096 × 32 | 647.7 | 583.0 (−10%) | **691.1 (+7%)** |
| 16384 × 1 | 84.2 | 68.0 (−19%) | 83.8 (−0%) |
| 16384 × 8 | 192.1 | 159.7 (−17%) | 144.5 (−25%)† |
| 16384 × 32 | 255.5 | 216.0 (−15%) | 233.5 (−9%) |
| 32768 × 8 | 132.9 | 104.8 (−21%) | 131.5 (−1%) |
| 32768 × 32 | 188.1 | 152.3 (−19%) | 107.2 (−43%)† |
| 131072 × 32 (4.2M live tokens, oversubscribes bf16 capacity) | 18,721 total tok/s, 224 s | 14,842 total tok/s, 283 s (−21%) | **19,030 total tok/s, 221 s (+2%)**; 0 preemptions on all three (scheduler queues) |

Latency split, same runs (mean TTFT / median ITL, ms):

| ISL × conc | TTFT bf16 | TTFT nvfp4 | TTFT fp8 | ITL bf16 | ITL nvfp4 | ITL fp8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 × 1 | 301 | 358 (+19%) | 303 (+1%) | 4.91 | 5.19 (+6%) | 4.92 (+0%) |
| 4096 × 8 | 956 | 1,214 (+27%) | 1,164 (+22%) | 5.24 | 5.75 (+10%) | 5.60 (+7%) |
| 4096 × 32 | 2,172 | 2,461 (+13%) | 2,111 (−3%) | 7.60 | 7.67 (+1%) | 8.20 (+8%) |
| 16384 × 1 | 907 | 1,217 (+34%) | 897 (−1%) | 5.07 | 5.43 (+7%) | 5.14 (+1%) |
| 16384 × 8 | 2,515 | 3,125 (+24%) | 3,410 (+36%)† | 5.60 | 5.58 (−0%) | 5.38 (−4%)† |
| 16384 × 32 | 6,370 | 7,572 (+19%) | 6,942 (+9%) | 86.8 | 111.9 (+29%) | **85.3 (−2%)** |
| 32768 × 8 | 4,177 | 5,357 (+28%) | 4,163 (−0%) | 5.91 | 5.50 (−7%) | 5.62 (−5%) |
| 32768 × 32 | 9,077 | 10,441 (+15%) | 21,031 (+132%)† | 103.2 | 124.7 (+21%) | **88.7 (−14%)†** |
| 131072 × 32 | 110,380 | 147,158 (+33%) | 110,984 (+1%) | 118.7 | 175.2 (+48%) | 126.1 (+6%) |

† fp8 cells at 16384×8 / 32768×32 are means of two independent runs (fresh server, warmup): 140.1/148.8 and 111.3/103.1 out tok/s, 3,495/3,325 and 20,522/21,540 ms TTFT — the prefill blowup reproduced both times, so it is a real property of the fmha_v2 fp8 sink-prefill path on these shapes, not a cold-start artifact.

Reading the split: **nvfp4's cost is symmetric but modest** — prefill TTFT +13–34%, and decode ITL from parity at low concurrency up to +48% (gap widens with ISL×conc, i.e. in-kernel fp4 dequant per read) — and what it buys is capacity/context (3.55× pool; unique dtype that serves a 209k-token request at TP=1). **fp8's cost is prefill-only and non-monotonic**: TTFT within ±10% of bf16 at 6/9 points including both long-context extremes (131k×32: 111.0 s vs 110.4 s bf16, vs 147.2 s nvfp4), blowups only at the two mid-ISL points above; on decode, fp8 ITL is bf16-equal at low concurrency and the fastest of the three at high concurrency × long ISL. This matches the independent 5060 Ti numbers below (decode flat/faster, cold prefill within a few % at 12k–153k); it also matches the one prior data point we know — #60452 (XQA NVFP4 decode enablement) measured NVFP4 KV slower than fp8 on 5060 Ti (58.2 vs 60.9 tok/s).

- **Independent reproduction** — [@paulocarinhena](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63826#issuecomment-6429067916) (issue author), 2× RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (SM120, TP=2, 2.5 GiB/GPU KV budget, prefix caching):

| | bf16 | nvfp4 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| KV pool (tokens) | 169,683 | **625,340** | **3.69×** |
| 262,144-token requests fittable | no (max 163,840) | yes, 2.39× | — |
| decode tok/s @ 85k cached ctx | 119 | 150 | **+26%** |
| decode tok/s @ 153k cached ctx | 92 | 132 | **+43%** |
| decode tok/s @ 250k ctx | does not fit | 113 | — |
| cold prefill tok/s @ 12k–153k | 6,992 → 3,109 | 6,736 → 2,934 | −4% to −6% |
| short-context serving, 8 conc | 773 | 781 | within noise |

  plus two concurrent 200,634-token prompts (~402k live tokens) finished side by side with no preemption/OOM; needle-retrieval limits unchanged by nvfp4 (identical pass/fail pattern at 12k–250k); tool calling and reasoning identical. On a bandwidth-limited card, reading 4-bit K/V more than pays for the dequant once context is long — the opposite regime from the 5090 grid, and exactly the setup this PR targets.

## Details

**Root cause.** `BatchAttentionWithAttentionSinkWrapper` cannot read packed NVFP4 pages (pre-existing rejection). The plain fa2 paged wrapper *does* read them on SM12x via JIT but silently ignores `sinks=` (verified empirically) — while supporting `return_lse=True`. The sink contributes denominator mass `exp(sink)`; fa2's LSE is log2-domain, so `out * sigmoid(ln2 * lse − sinks)` is exact (one multiply in fp32, `out=` in place).

**Gating.** On SM12x, decode runs XQA, which applies sinks natively; off SM12x decode would land on the plain fa2 decode wrapper, probed to silently ignore `sinks=`. Hence the rejection for device major != 12 in both `supports_combination` and the builder, and the SM12x gate additionally keyed on the resolved decode kernel (XQA revert → raise). Holds until a sink-capable decode wrapper ships (#6021, merged but unreleased) and is validated off-12x.

**Flint side.** Flint's fused `qk_norm_rope` kernel writes the KV cache through bf16 views, which don't apply to quantized packed layouts, so for any non-bf16 `kv_cache_dtype` the model routes through `unified_kv_cache_update` — one shared `impl_owns_kv_cache` flag drives the assert, the custom-decode gate, the forward path, and `_cache_views` (also fixes a pre-existing `== "nvfp4"` vs `startswith` inconsistency). This is what unblocks fp8 as a side effect. bf16 serving is unchanged (same kernels, same paths; the bf16 GSM8K row was measured on this branch).

**Adjacent work (not duplicates).** #63169 opens fa2 NVFP4 at head_size 64 but keeps the sink rejection — this PR does the reverse, disjoint. #59878 opens sink wrappers for SM8x and, in its latest revision, also routes NVFP4+sinks through FlashInfer's sink prefill/decode wrappers — but those wrappers come from flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6021, which is merged yet unreleased: vLLM pins flashinfer 0.7.2.post1, where `BatchDecodeWithAttentionSinkWrapper` does not exist (top-level `from flashinfer import` fails outright) and the sink prefill wrapper has no functional `kv_cache_sf` support, so that NVFP4 path cannot run until a flashinfer release ships #6021 and vLLM bumps the pin. This PR's epilogue approach works on the pinned release today, SM12x-only. #53979 built the fa2 NVFP4 prefill path this rides on. #60452 added XQA NVFP4 decode (enablement precedent).

**Scope notes.** NVFP4 KV cache itself remains undocumented in `docs/features/quantization/quantized_kvcache.md` (pre-existing gap — happy to add a section if reviewers want one). flashinfer quirk noted for reviewers: on the pinned 0.7.2.post1 the sink-wrapper JIT URI lacks head dims, so head_dim-128 and 256 wrappers in one process share a compiled module and one returns wrong output — already fixed upstream in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6021 (unreleased); the CI selector above avoids co-selecting them. Bench/eval numbers: bf16/nvfp4 at a22868a, fp8 at e7002bd4f2 (the pre-rebase tip; the later rebase onto main b71c1d5f14 changed only the CI selector line, no code, so the numbers carry over). The two review-round commits (d813a759: fp32 epilogue rounding + arch gate; e7002bd: gate on resolved decode kernel + reject test + LSE layout pinned in the epilogue comment) likewise change no math.

AI assistance was used (Claude Code) for implementation, testing and benchmarking; every changed line was reviewed and all validations above were run by the human submitter on the pod configuration described.

Thanks a lot @grYe99 for picking this up so quickly, and for the clear write-up. I tested the PR on a smaller SM120 setup than yours, with TP=2. Short version: it works end to end; capacity goes up 3.7× with no quality loss I could measure; and on this GPU decode at long context is actually *faster* than bf16.

### Setup

- 2× RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (sm_120, 448 GB/s each), TP=2, `--disable-custom-all-reduce`
- PR head `c6a1439e` applied on top of nightly `0.32.1rc1.dev486+g0765565f1`. Only the `vllm/models/flint/model.py` and `flashinfer.py` hunks were applied; both applied cleanly, with line offsets.
- FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, torch 2.14.0+cu130
- `RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf` with `--hf-config-path`/`--tokenizer` from the BF16 repo
- `--kv-cache-memory 2684354560` (2.5 GiB/GPU), `--max-num-seqs 8`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 2560`, prefix caching, glm47 tool and reasoning parsers

Weights take ~11 GiB of the 15.5 GiB on each GPU, so the KV budget is small. That is exactly the case this PR targets.

### Capacity (same 2.5 GiB/GPU KV budget)

| KV dtype | KV pool | 262,144-token requests |
|---|---|---|
| bf16 (main) | 169,683 tokens | does not fit; max-model-len 163,840 |
| fp8 (local patch, see note 2) | 351,744 tokens | 1.34× |
| **nvfp4 (this PR)** | **625,340 tokens (3.69× bf16)** | **2.39×** |

Two concurrent requests of 200,634 prompt tokens each, plus 512 generated each (~402k live tokens), finished side by side in 169 s:
- KV usage peaked at 61%;
- no preemption and no OOM;
- the server stayed healthy.

### Speed: A/B on the same build, bf16 vs nvfp4 KV

Decode at cached long context (streaming, `ignore_eos`, 1,024 tokens, batch 1):

| context | bf16 | nvfp4 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12k | 176 tok/s | 177 tok/s | 0% |
| 85k | 119 tok/s | 150 tok/s | **+26%** |
| 153k | 92 tok/s | 132 tok/s | **+43%** |
| 250k | does not fit | 113 tok/s | n/a |

The nvfp4 numbers are from a second run. On the first run (right after startup, which includes JIT warm-up) nvfp4 measured 150 / 116 / 132 tok/s at 12k / 85k / 153k. So 153k was stable across runs, but treat the 85k gain as noisy.

Cold prefill (`max_tokens=1`, unique prefix):

| context | bf16 | nvfp4 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12k | 6,992 tok/s | 6,736 tok/s | −4% |
| 43k | 5,590 tok/s | 5,339 tok/s | −4% |
| 85k | 4,281 tok/s | 4,076 tok/s | −5% |
| 136k | 3,341 tok/s | 3,155 tok/s | −6% |
| 153k | 3,109 tok/s | 2,934 tok/s | −6% |

Short-context serving:
- 8 concurrent requests: 773 tok/s (bf16) vs 781 tok/s (nvfp4) aggregate;
- single request: 189 vs 180 tok/s, within run-to-run noise (~±5%).

My guess is that on a bandwidth-limited card like the 5060 Ti, reading 4-bit K/V more than pays for the in-kernel dequant once the context is long. That would fit your 5090/TP4 grid showing a slowdown (more bandwidth, higher concurrency) while this shows a speedup. One sample per point, so treat the exact percentages as approximate.

### Quality

- **Needle retrieval:** a code word in the middle of repeated Portuguese filler, neutral prompt. bf16 and nvfp4 behave the same: both find it at 12k, 43k and 85k, and both fail at 136k and 153k. bf16 failed 2 of 2 attempts at both of those lengths. nvfp4 also fails at 200k and 250k. So the long-context limit here is the model's own, and I saw no extra degradation from nvfp4 KV.
- **Tool calling and reasoning:** tool calls (glm47), reasoning extraction and a short math word problem all behave the same on both.

### Review notes

1. **SM8x/SM90 decode with sinks + NVFP4.** I'm not sure this is safe. On SM120 decode goes through XQA (`can_use_xqa_or_trtllm_gen_decode` is True for `nvfp4_fa2` on family 120), and XQA applies the sinks, which matches my results. But the PR also opens `has_sink + nvfp4` for SM8x/SM9x, both in `supports_combination` and in the `__init__` check. There, decode falls back to `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(use_tensor_cores=True)` on fa2. In FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 that path calls the same fa2 `paged_run` that you found silently ignores `sinks=` in prefill. If so, SM8x/SM90 would decode without the sink and give wrong output with no error. I can't test SM8x/SM90 here. Options: restrict the gate to SM12x (the only arch validated), or apply the same LSE epilogue in the fa2 decode path and add a decode test there.
2. **fp8 KV for Flint.** The model-side change (`k_cache=None` in `qk_norm_rope_cache`, then `unified_kv_cache_update`) is exactly what I had done locally for fp8. It works on SM120 with the stock sink wrappers: 351,744-token pool, same speed as bf16, coherent output. Could the Flint check be generalized from `nvfp4` to "any non-bf16 KV dtype"? That would be `self.attn.kv_cache_dtype not in ("auto", "bfloat16")`, both for the assert/`flint_decode` gate and in `_cache_views`. Then fp8 works too, with no extra code. `_cache_views` checks `== "nvfp4"` while `forward` checks `self.impl.is_kvcache_nvfp4` (`startswith("nvfp4")`), so a single shared flag would also keep the two in sync.
3. **Nit.** `sink_corr.to(out_pre.dtype)` rounds the correction to bf16 before the multiply. Doing the multiply in fp32 and casting once avoids that extra rounding. Running the wrapper with `out=out_prefill` and an in-place `mul_` would also save the temporary and the `copy_`.

Thanks again! Happy to re-run any of this on the 5060 Ti setup if you change the gating.

Thanks for the careful review — all three points are addressed in d813a759 (just pushed). Details below.

**1. SM8x/SM90 decode.** Confirmed your suspicion with a direct probe on flashinfer 0.7.2.post1: a plain `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(use_tensor_cores=True, backend="fa2")` accepts `run(q, kv, sinks=...)` without error, but the output is **bit-identical** to a sinks-free run (`torch.equal` → True), and it matches a sink-less fp32 oracle rather than the sink oracle — i.e. sinks are silently ignored on that path, exactly as you feared. So the combination is now gated to SM12x in both places:

- `supports_combination` rejects `has_sink + nvfp4` unless `device_capability.major == 12` (head-64 rejection unchanged).
- The builder `__init__` rejects `has_sinks` when `nvfp4_fa2 and not device_family(120)`; the nvfp4_trtllm/SM100 route is untouched, and SM12x without XQA still rejects via `supports_sink()`.

I picked the gate over adding an fa2-decode epilogue because neither of us has SM8x/SM90 hardware to validate it on, and that fallback decode path is shared by many more configurations — a wrong-both-ways risk without coverage. The comments point at `BatchDecodeWithAttentionSinkWrapper` (flashinfer #6021, merged, unreleased) as the way to reopen those archs once it ships and is validated. The comments point at `BatchDecodeWithAttentionSinkWrapper` (flashinfer #6021, merged, unreleased) as the way to reopen those archs once it ships and is validated.

**2. fp8 generalization.** Adopted exactly as suggested — one shared flag:

```python
self.impl_owns_kv_cache = self.attn.kv_cache_dtype not in ("auto", "bfloat16")
self.flint_decode = _flint_kernels(quant_config) and not self.impl_owns_kv_cache
```

It now drives the old assert site, the `flint_decode` gate, the forward routing through `unified_kv_cache_update`, and `_cache_views` — which also removes the `== "nvfp4"` vs `is_kvcache_nvfp4` (`startswith`) skew you spotted. Validated on SM120 at this tip: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` serves the GGUF end-to-end, KV pool **424,435 tokens** (max-model-len 262144, util 0.92), chat smoke coherent. (My first smoke attempt died on a mundane config bug — main needs `--tokenizer RecursiveSI/flint` alongside a GGUF `--model` since `get_tokenizer` moved to `vllm/tokenizers/`; fixed and re-ran green.)

**3. Rounding nit.** Done — the wrapper now writes straight into `out_prefill` (`out=`) and `sink_corr` stays fp32, so `mul_` promotes and the correction rounds exactly once; the temporary and the `copy_` are gone. (`out=` works fine on the plain prefill wrapper in 0.7.2.post1; the sink unit tests exercise that path end-to-end.)

**Re-validation at the new tip** (RTX 5090): `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py -k nvfp4 -v` → **6 passed, 156 deselected in 37.55s** (4 pre-existing NVFP4 decode params + the 2 new sink tests). GSM8K/serving numbers in the description predate this commit, which changes only the epilogue's rounding mode and the arch gate, not the algorithm.

One extra thing worth flagging on the buildkite one-liner: `-k` is substring matching, and the previous selector `test_flashinfer_xqa_nvfp4_decode_correctness` matched **zero tests** — #60532 (71e9320633) renamed that test to `test_flashinfer_nvfp4_decode_correctness` without updating the yaml, so the dgx-spark step has been silently selecting nothing. `-k nvfp4` restores that coverage and picks up the new sink tests. Happy to tighten it to `-k "nvfp4_decode_correctness or nvfp4_sink_prefill"` if you prefer a narrower selection.

Your note that #59878 doesn't touch NVFP4 made me realize I'd left it out by mistake, thanks for that! It's added now: sinks with an NVFP4 KV cache go through FlashInfer's sink prefill and decode wrappers there.

## Details

**Root cause.** `BatchAttentionWithAttentionSinkWrapper` cannot read packed NVFP4 pages (pre-existing rejection). The plain fa2 paged wrapper *does* read them on SM12x via JIT but silently ignores `sinks=` (verified empirically) — while supporting `return_lse=True`. The sink contributes denominator mass `exp(sink)`; fa2's LSE is log2-domain, so `out * sigmoid(ln2 * lse − sinks)` is exact (one multiply in fp32, `out=` in place).

**Gating.** On SM12x, decode runs XQA, which applies sinks natively; off SM12x decode would land on the plain fa2 decode wrapper, probed to silently ignore `sinks=`. Hence the rejection for device major != 12 in both `supports_combination` and the builder, and the SM12x gate additionally keyed on the resolved decode kernel (XQA revert → raise). Holds until a sink-capable decode wrapper ships (#6021, merged but unreleased) and is validated off-12x.

**Flint side.** Flint's fused `qk_norm_rope` kernel writes the KV cache through bf16 views, which don't apply to quantized packed layouts, so for any non-bf16 `kv_cache_dtype` the model routes through `unified_kv_cache_update` — one shared `impl_owns_kv_cache` flag drives the assert, the custom-decode gate, the forward path, and `_cache_views` (also fixes a pre-existing `== "nvfp4"` vs `startswith` inconsistency). This PR's epilogue approach works on the pinned release today, SM12x-only. #53979 built the fa2 NVFP4 prefill path this rides on. #60452 added XQA NVFP4 decode (enablement precedent).

**Scope notes.** NVFP4 KV cache itself remains undocumented in `docs/features/quantization/quantized_kvcache.md` (pre-existing gap — happy to add a section if reviewers want one). flashinfer quirk noted for reviewers: on the pinned 0.7.2.post1 the sink-wrapper JIT URI lacks head dims, so head_dim-128 and 256 wrappers in one process share a compiled module and one returns wrong output — already fixed upstream in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6021 (unreleased); the CI selector above avoids co-selecting them. +@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_cuda_graph", [False, True])
+def test_flashinfer_nvfp4_sink_prefill_correctness(default_vllm_config, use_cuda_graph):
+    """Sinks over an NVFP4 paged cache match an SDPA-with-sink oracle.
+
+    On SM12x the NVFP4 route serves prefill with the plain fa2 paged wrapper
+    at return_lse=True plus the out * sigmoid(ln2 * lse - sinks) epilogue,
+    eager and under CUDA-graph capture. Each route is checked against an fp32
+    SDPA-with-sink oracle over that route's own effective K/V: exact bf16 for
+    the sink-wrapper route, and the dequantized NVFP4 cache contents for the
+    fa2 route, so the check covers sink routing plus the kernel's read/write
+    quantization convention instead of baking random-input quantization error
+    into the tolerance. The batch mixes a long-context single-token request
+    (decode), two pure prefills, and a long-context short extend.
+    """
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    # Decode-class requests must come first in the batch.
+    seq_lens, bs, d = [300, 40, 1027, 512], 16, 256
+    config = create_vllm_config(
+        model_name="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
+        max_model_len=max(seq_lens),
+        block_size=bs,
+        dtype="bfloat16",
+    )
+    # GQA 6 at head_dim 256, as in test_flashinfer_nvfp4_decode_correctness.
+    config.model_config.model_arch_config = replace(
+        config.model_config.model_arch_config,
+        total_num_attention_heads=24,
+        total_num_kv_heads=4,
+        head_size=d,
+    )
+    device = torch.device(f"{DEVICE_TYPE}:0")
+    q, k, v = (
+        torch.randn(sum(seq_lens), h, d).bfloat16().to(device) for h in (24, 4, 4)
+    )
+    sinks = torch.rand(24, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) * 2.0 - 0.5
+
+    # Request i owns consecutive pages from starts[i]; page 0 stays null.
+    pages = [0] + [cdiv(s, bs) for s in seq_lens[:-1]]
+    starts = 1 + torch.tensor(pages).cumsum(0)
+    max_pages = cdiv(max(seq_lens), bs)
+    block_table = (starts[:, None] + torch.arange(max_pages)).int().to(device)
+    num_pages = int(starts[-1]) + max_pages
+    full_dim = nvfp4_kv_cache_full_dim(d)
+    caches = {
+        "nvfp4": torch.zeros(
+            num_pages, bs, 8, full_dim, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device
+        ).transpose(1, 2),
+        "auto": torch.zeros(
+            num_pages, bs, 4, 2 * d, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
+        ).transpose(1, 2),
+    }
+
+    def run(query_lens, kv_cache_dtype, use_cuda_graph=False):
+        is_nvfp4 = kv_cache_dtype == "nvfp4"
+        config.cache_config.cache_dtype = kv_cache_dtype
+        spec = FullAttentionSpec(
+            block_size=bs,
+            num_kv_heads=4,
+            head_size=d,
+            dtype=torch.uint8 if is_nvfp4 else torch.bfloat16,
+            kv_quant_mode=KVQuantMode.NVFP4 if is_nvfp4 else KVQuantMode.NONE,
+        )
+        req = torch.repeat_interleave(torch.arange(4), torch.tensor(query_lens))
+        pos = torch.cat([torch.arange(s - n, s) for s, n in zip(seq_lens, query_lens)])
+        rows = pos + torch.tensor([0, *seq_lens]).cumsum(0)[req]
+        metadata = replace(
+            create_common_attn_metadata(BatchSpec(seq_lens, query_lens), bs, device),
+            block_table_tensor=block_table,
+            slot_mapping=(starts[req] * bs + pos).to(device),
+        )
+        with set_current_vllm_config(config):
+            return rows, run_attention_backend(
+                AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHINFER,
+                spec,
+                ["placeholder"],
+                config,
+                device,
+                metadata,
+                q[rows],
+                k[rows],
+                v[rows],
+                caches[kv_cache_dtype],
+                kv_cache_dtype=kv_cache_dtype,
+                sinks=sinks,
+                use_cuda_graph=use_cuda_graph,
+                # gs rides the layer scales in the real nvfp4 model path;
+                # bf16 layers keep the default unit scales.
+                layer_k_scale=0.02 if is_nvfp4 else 1.0,
+                layer_v_scale=0.03 if is_nvfp4 else 1.0,
+            )
+
+    # Each route is checked against an fp32 SDPA-with-sink oracle over that
+    # route's own effective K/V. The NVFP4 oracle reads the dequantized cache
+    # contents: lo nibble at even elements, per-16-element block scale
+    # e4m3(amax / (6 * gs)), dequantized value q * sc * gs (all measured
+    # against the quantize-append kernel on SM120).
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.flashinfer import _nvfp4_kv_views
+
+    e2m1 = torch.tensor(
+        [0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0]
+        + [0.0, -0.5, -1.0, -1.5, -2.0, -3.0, -4.0, -6.0],
+        device=device,
+    )
+    req_idx = torch.repeat_interleave(
+        torch.arange(4, device=device), torch.tensor(seq_lens, device=device)
+    )
+    tok_pos = torch.cat([torch.arange(s, device=device) for s in seq_lens])
+    tok_page = block_table.long()[req_idx, tok_pos // bs]
+    tok_off = tok_pos % bs
+
+    def dequant_cache(data, scales, gs):
+        packed = data[tok_page, tok_off].long()
+        q_vals = torch.stack((e2m1[packed & 0xF], e2m1[(packed >> 4) & 0xF]), dim=-1)
+        blk_scale = scales[tok_page, tok_off].float().repeat_interleave(16, dim=-1)
+        return q_vals.flatten(2) * blk_scale * gs
+
+    sm_scale = d**-0.5
+    bounds = [0, *torch.tensor(seq_lens).cumsum(0).tolist()]
+
+    def sdpa_with_sinks(q_rows, k_eff, v_eff, query_lens):
+        outs, row = [], 0
+        for r, (s, n) in enumerate(zip(seq_lens, query_lens)):
+            qi = q_rows[row : row + n].float()
+            ki = k_eff[bounds[r] : bounds[r + 1]].repeat_interleave(6, dim=1).float()
+            vi = v_eff[bounds[r] : bounds[r + 1]].repeat_interleave(6, dim=1).float()
+            scores = torch.einsum("nhd,shd->hns", qi, ki) * sm_scale
+            kv_idx = torch.arange(s, device=device)
+            q_idx = torch.arange(s - n, s, device=device)
+            scores.masked_fill_(kv_idx[None, :] > q_idx[:, None], float("-inf"))
+            sink_col = sinks.view(-1, 1, 1).expand(-1, n, -1)
+            weights = torch.softmax(torch.cat((scores, sink_col), dim=-1), dim=-1)
+            outs.append(torch.einsum("hns,shd->nhd", weights[..., :s], vi))
+            row += n
+        return torch.cat(outs)
+
+    # A full prefill per route writes every token through its cache; the
+    # incremental phase only rewrites the same values at the same slots, so
+    # one NVFP4 readout feeds all oracles.
+    _, out_full_nvfp4 = run(seq_lens, "nvfp4")
+    _, out_full_bf16 = run(seq_lens, "auto")
+    (k_data, v_data), (k_scale, v_scale), _ = _nvfp4_kv_views(caches["nvfp4"], 4)
+    k_fp4 = dequant_cache(k_data, k_scale, 0.02)
+    v_fp4 = dequant_cache(v_data, v_scale, 0.03)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        out_full_bf16.float(),
+        sdpa_with_sinks(q, k, v, seq_lens),
+        atol=2e-2,
+        rtol=2e-2,
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        out_full_nvfp4.float(),
+        sdpa_with_sinks(q, k_fp4, v_fp4, seq_lens),
+        atol=2e-2,
+        rtol=2e-2,
+    )
+
+    mixed_query_lens = [1, 40, 1027, 8]
+    rows, out_nvfp4 = run(mixed_query_lens, "nvfp4", use_cuda_graph)
+    _, out_bf16 = run(mixed_query_lens, "auto", use_cuda_graph)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        out_bf16.float(),
+        sdpa_with_sinks(q[rows], k, v, mixed_query_lens),
+        atol=2e-2,
+        rtol=2e-2,
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        out_nvfp4.float(),
+        sdpa_with_sinks(q[rows], k_fp4, v_fp4, mixed_query_lens),
+        atol=2e-2,
+        rtol=2e-2,
+    )
+

Thanks a lot @grYe99 for picking this up so quickly, and for the clear write-up. I tested the PR on a smaller SM120 setup than yours, with TP=2. Short version: it works end to end; capacity goes up 3.7× with no quality loss I could measure; and on this GPU decode at long context is actually *faster* than bf16.

### Setup

- 2× RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (sm_120, 448 GB/s each), TP=2, `--disable-custom-all-reduce`
- PR head `c6a1439e` applied on top of nightly `0.32.1rc1.dev486+g0765565f1`. Only the `vllm/models/flint/model.py` and `flashinfer.py` hunks were applied; both applied cleanly, with line offsets.
- FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, torch 2.14.0+cu130
- `RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf` with `--hf-config-path`/`--tokenizer` from the BF16 repo
- `--kv-cache-memory 2684354560` (2.5 GiB/GPU), `--max-num-seqs 8`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 2560`, prefix caching, glm47 tool and reasoning parsers

Weights take ~11 GiB of the 15.5 GiB on each GPU, so the KV budget is small. That is exactly the case this PR targets.

### Capacity (same 2.5 GiB/GPU KV budget)

| KV dtype | KV pool | 262,144-token requests |
|---|---|---|
| bf16 (main) | 169,683 tokens | does not fit; max-model-len 163,840 |
| fp8 (local patch, see note 2) | 351,744 tokens | 1.34× |
| **nvfp4 (this PR)** | **625,340 tokens (3.69× bf16)** | **2.39×** |

Two concurrent requests of 200,634 prompt tokens each, plus 512 generated each (~402k live tokens), finished side by side in 169 s:
- KV usage peaked at 61%;
- no preemption and no OOM;
- the server stayed healthy.

### Speed: A/B on the same build, bf16 vs nvfp4 KV

Decode at cached long context (streaming, `ignore_eos`, 1,024 tokens, batch 1):

| context | bf16 | nvfp4 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12k | 176 tok/s | 177 tok/s | 0% |
| 85k | 119 tok/s | 150 tok/s | **+26%** |
| 153k | 92 tok/s | 132 tok/s | **+43%** |
| 250k | does not fit | 113 tok/s | n/a |

The nvfp4 numbers are from a second run. On the first run (right after startup, which includes JIT warm-up) nvfp4 measured 150 / 116 / 132 tok/s at 12k / 85k / 153k. So 153k was stable across runs, but treat the 85k gain as noisy.

Cold prefill (`max_tokens=1`, unique prefix):

| context | bf16 | nvfp4 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12k | 6,992 tok/s | 6,736 tok/s | −4% |
| 43k | 5,590 tok/s | 5,339 tok/s | −4% |
| 85k | 4,281 tok/s | 4,076 tok/s | −5% |
| 136k | 3,341 tok/s | 3,155 tok/s | −6% |
| 153k | 3,109 tok/s | 2,934 tok/s | −6% |

Short-context serving:
- 8 concurrent requests: 773 tok/s (bf16) vs 781 tok/s (nvfp4) aggregate;
- single request: 189 vs 180 tok/s, within run-to-run noise (~±5%).

My guess is that on a bandwidth-limited card like the 5060 Ti, reading 4-bit K/V more than pays for the in-kernel dequant once the context is long. That would fit your 5090/TP4 grid showing a slowdown (more bandwidth, higher concurrency) while this shows a speedup. One sample per point, so treat the exact percentages as approximate.

### Quality

- **Needle retrieval:** a code word in the middle of repeated Portuguese filler, neutral prompt. bf16 and nvfp4 behave the same: both find it at 12k, 43k and 85k, and both fail at 136k and 153k. bf16 failed 2 of 2 attempts at both of those lengths. nvfp4 also fails at 200k and 250k. So the long-context limit here is the model's own, and I saw no extra degradation from nvfp4 KV.
- **Tool calling and reasoning:** tool calls (glm47), reasoning extraction and a short math word problem all behave the same on both.

### Review notes

1. **SM8x/SM90 decode with sinks + NVFP4.** I'm not sure this is safe. On SM120 decode goes through XQA (`can_use_xqa_or_trtllm_gen_decode` is True for `nvfp4_fa2` on family 120), and XQA applies the sinks, which matches my results. But the PR also opens `has_sink + nvfp4` for SM8x/SM9x, both in `supports_combination` and in the `__init__` check. There, decode falls back to `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(use_tensor_cores=True)` on fa2. In FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 that path calls the same fa2 `paged_run` that you found silently ignores `sinks=` in prefill. If so, SM8x/SM90 would decode without the sink and give wrong output with no error. I can't test SM8x/SM90 here. Options: restrict the gate to SM12x (the only arch validated), or apply the same LSE epilogue in the fa2 decode path and add a decode test there.
2. **fp8 KV for Flint.** The model-side change (`k_cache=None` in `qk_norm_rope_cache`, then `unified_kv_cache_update`) is exactly what I had done locally for fp8. It works on SM120 with the stock sink wrappers: 351,744-token pool, same speed as bf16, coherent output. Could the Flint check be generalized from `nvfp4` to "any non-bf16 KV dtype"? That would be `self.attn.kv_cache_dtype not in ("auto", "bfloat16")`, both for the assert/`flint_decode` gate and in `_cache_views`. Then fp8 works too, with no extra code. `_cache_views` checks `== "nvfp4"` while `forward` checks `self.impl.is_kvcache_nvfp4` (`startswith("nvfp4")`), so a single shared flag would also keep the two in sync.
3. **Nit.** `sink_corr.to(out_pre.dtype)` rounds the correction to bf16 before the multiply. Doing the multiply in fp32 and casting once avoids that extra rounding. Running the wrapper with `out=out_prefill` and an in-place `mul_` would also save the temporary and the `copy_`.

Thanks again! Happy to re-run any of this on the 5060 Ti setup if you change the gating.
